concerns.text: FR-002 still reads 'scaffold-based split with fixed ratios [deferred] train, [deferred] validation, [deferred] test'. The 80/10/10 ratio is a constitution-mandated constant (Principle VI: 'MUST enforce a scaffold-based data split (80% train, 10% validation, 10% test)'), not an empirical value to defer. Note FR-013 already asserts the 80/10/10 ratios, so FR-002 is also internally inconsistent. Restore explicit 80/10/10 in FR-002.

The assumption text still carries a literal '[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]' marker ('a `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` marker will be used'). Even as a described future convention, a converged spec should not contain this token; rephrase to a concrete fallback (e.g., 'datasets lacking FQY values are rejected at ingestion with a logged reason').

FR-002 states 'scaffold-based split with fixed ratios [deferred] train, [deferred] validation, [deferred] test' while FR-013 states the system 'does not alter the 80/10/10 split ratios'. The two FRs are mutually incompatible: FR-002 leaves the ratios undefined while FR-013 hard-codes 80/10/10. Restore the explicit 80/10/10 ratios in FR-002 (also mandated by Constitution Principle VI) so both FRs agree.
FR IDs jump from FR-013 to FR-015 with no FR-014. If FR-014 was removed during revision, renumber or note the gap; as-is, cross-reference consumers may treat the missing ID as a dangling reference.

FR-002 uses a '[deferred]' placeholder for the train/validation/test split ratios. The Constitution (Principle VI) mandates an explicit 80/10/10 split. Without concrete ratios the split cannot be measured, making the requirement untestable.

The document contains a '[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]' marker in the assumptions section ("if a specific dataset lacks experimental FQY values, a `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` marker will be used"). A converged spec must not contain any such placeholder; its presence leaves the requirement undefined and untestable.

Acceptance Scenario 3 references a molecule selected from the "top [deferred] experimental FQY of the test set". The placeholder prevents the scenario from being reproducibly instantiated, so the test cannot be executed. Replace the placeholder with a concrete selection rule (e.g., top‑5 % highest FQY values).

FR-002 reads 'scaffold‑based split ([deferred] train, [deferred] validation, [deferred] test)'. The constitution (Principle VI) and the original idea both mandate explicit 80/10/10 split ratios. Using [deferred] under‑reaches the required constant and risks violating the scaffold‑based generalizability rule.
A '[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]' marker remains in the specification. All such placeholders must be resolved before the spec can be considered converged.

The idea states an expected predictive performance of R² ≥ 0.7, yet SC‑001 only requires measuring R² without specifying a target threshold. This under‑reaches the idea’s claim and leaves the primary hypothesis untested.

FR-010 mandates min-max normalization of FQY but never states the scaling statistics are computed on the TRAINING set only. If min/max are fit on the pooled dataset, test-set target information leaks into preprocessing — undermining the scaffold-disjoint validation the whole design rests on (Constitution VI). Specify train-fit-only scaling.

FR-012 skips any molecule with atom/bond types unseen in training. Applied at evaluation time this selectively drops test molecules based on training-set content, biasing the reported R²/RMSE/MAE (the test set is no longer the scaffold-split sample). Skipping should apply at inference on new inputs, not to held-out evaluation molecules; at minimum require logging and reporting of dropped test fraction.

The interpretability validation hinges on a 'curated reference set of fluorophore motifs (Supplementary Table S1)' whose provenance, construction rule, and independence from the model's training data are entirely unspecified. If the motif list is assembled post hoc from the same chemistry the attributions highlight, the ≥60% overlap check becomes near-tautological. Define the source/selection rule for Table S1 and its independence from the attribution pipeline.

FR-015 records solvent/temperature/method metadata but no FR uses it. FQY is strongly condition-dependent; pooling measurements across solvents/temperatures adds target noise the spec should at least acknowledge (e.g., report condition heterogeneity or restrict to a dominant condition) — otherwise the metadata requirement is scientifically inert.
